honing_confound: Surge Enhancement at 60-stack doubles the Surge skill damage — this compounds with Specialization (gear honing). At T4, peak Specialization makes the single 60-stack Surge hit the highest single-skill damage moment in the Deathblade's kit. The floor-to-ceiling gap for Surge is large: under-stacking (e.g., Surge at 30 stacks) yields ~half the ceiling output. Tier standing reflects maximum-honing optimized ceiling.

delivery.evidence: Deathblade is a melee assassin using dark-infused blade skills (Wind Cut, Surprise Attack, Blade Dance, Blitz Rush as primary stackers; Surge as the burst skill). All skills delivered at close melee range via dash-in positioning.

footprint.evidence: Blade-arc melee skills: small cone or narrow arc footprints. Surge itself is a close-range dark energy release. No wide-zone AoE identity.

geo_text: Surge Deathblade manages three Death Orbs (filled via combat). Activating Death Trance (Z) consumes Orbs granting: Attack Speed +10/15/20%, Move Speed +10%, Attack Power +8/16/24%, -50% Cooldown on activation. During Death Trance: every skill hit stacks Surge Enhancement (max 60). At 60 stacks: Surge deals +90/120/170% bonus damage (Limit Break doubles the base 45/60/85% — the 60-stack threshold is the explicit optimization target). After Surge cast: Death Orbs refunded → immediate cycle restart.

control.evidence: Some Deathblade skills include knockdown on impact. No CC-centered identity.

defense.evidence: Glass-cannon assassin — no armor, purely mobility-based defense. High repositioning capability. Melee range creates inherent vulnerability.

economy.resource_verbatim: Death Orbs (3 max) + Surge Enhancement Stacks (60 max during Death Trance)
economy.builder_source: All skills fill Death Orbs. During Death Trance (Z active), all skill hits accumulate Surge Enhancement stacks.
economy.plain_text: DEATH ORB + SURGE ENHANCEMENT ECONOMY: Fill 3 Death Orbs via combat → Death Trance (Z) consumes Orbs for AS/AP/Cooldown buffs → during Death Trance: stack Surge Enhancement to max 60 via rapid multi-hit skills → cast Surge at 60 for Limit Break (double bonus = 90/120/170%) → Death Orbs refunded on Surge cast → immediate re-entry. SURGE IDENTITY: maximize stacking speed to 60 per cycle.

element.evidence: Deathblade uses dark-energy-infused blade strikes. Primarily Physical with Dark elemental flavor on signature skills including Surge itself.

movement.evidence: Deathblade is very mobile — multiple dash-stacker skills (Blitz Rush, Blade Dance include dash components). Back-attack positioning requires constant repositioning. Death Trance: +10% Move Speed.

attr.evidence: Pure melee assassin. Must stay within 0-5m for all significant damage output.

range.evidence: All Deathblade skills are close-range melee.

tempo.evidence: Surge identity = race to 60 stacks in Death Trance → single massive Surge detonation. Classic stacker-to-burst pattern with an explicit 60-stack threshold optimization.

amp.value: 60-stack Surge: +90/120/170% bonus damage; Death Trance: +8/16/24% Attack Power, +10/15/20% Attack Speed; back-attack: +10% Crit Rate +5% Damage
amp.evidence: Maxroll Surge guide: 'doubles to 90/120/170% when at the maximum 60 stacks.' Death Trance stats from same guide. Back-attack bonus from guide.

commitment.evidence: Surge has a cast animation (wind-up before dark energy release). Stacker skills are fast instants. Primary commitment moment is the Surge cast at 60 stacks.

mechanics_notes: 1) LIMIT BREAK THRESHOLD: at exactly 60 stacks, Surge damage doubles (45→90 / 60→120 / 85→170%). Under-stacking is a severe DPS loss — 59 stacks = half the ceiling output. This creates the highest optimization pressure of any Deathblade identity. 2) ORBS REFUNDED ON SURGE CAST: casting Surge at any stack count refunds Death Orbs → cycle restarts immediately. The timing of Surge cast (60 stacks vs sub-60) is the primary skill expression. 3) Back-attack positioning: Deathblade has Back Attack affixes on most skills (+10% Crit Rate +5% Damage from behind). This is implicit positioning requirement rather than explicit identity mandate but present throughout the skill pool. 4) SURGE vs REMAINING ENERGY META POSITION: Surge is B-tier (Maxroll Aug 2025) vs RE's S+ — the 60-stack requirement is punishing in mobile/dynamic raid content where interruptions reset stacks. Surge has higher theoretical ceiling but lower practical average.
stabilization_patch: Remaining Energy has been dominant since Ark Passive rework (Feb 2025); Surge fell to secondary choice.
tier_standing_release: A/S-tier at launch (Deathblade was top assassin at global launch; Surge was the meta identity initially)
tier_standing_current: B-tier (Maxroll community tier list August 2025). A-tier overall class (Manillagames January 2026). HONING-CONFOUND NOTE: 60-stack Surge peak requires T4 Specialization to deliver ceiling output; floor-to-ceiling gap is the largest of any Deathblade identity.

honing_confound: Remaining Energy's Attack Power bonus (+48% at 3 Orbs) stacks multiplicatively with Specialization (gear honing). The 30-second buff window means all skills fired during the window benefit from the compounded gear × identity multiplier. RE consistently outperforms Surge at all honing levels because the benefit is uniformly distributed (no single-spike optimization).

delivery.evidence: Same melee blade archetype as Surge. Surge (Z) activation, same skill pool. RE emphasizes rapid multi-skill firing within the 30-second buff window.

footprint.evidence: Same melee-arc blade footprint as Surge identity.

geo_text: Remaining Energy Deathblade fills 3 Death Orbs via combat → Surge (Z) consumes Orbs activating a 30-second power window: Attack Power +16/32/48% (1/2/3 Orbs), Cooldown Reduction -10/30/50% (excluding spacebar/Awakening), Max MP recovery +15/25/45%. During the 30-second window: fire all skills as fast as possible on halved cooldowns. After window: rebuild orbs, re-enter. REMAINING ENERGY IDENTITY: the peak is in sustained high-frequency skill output during the 30s window — 'constantly attacking with a multitude of skills.'

economy.plain_text: REMAINING ENERGY ECONOMY: Fill 3 Death Orbs → Surge (Z): +48% Attack Power + -50% Cooldown for 30 seconds. Within the window: fire all skills on reduced cooldowns for sustained burst. RE IDENTITY: maximize total skill hits within the 30s amplified window. No stack optimization required — output quality scales with how fully the 30s window is utilized.

movement.evidence: Same high-mobility profile. Move Speed +10% during Surge activation (same as Surge identity Death Trance).

tempo.evidence: RE is the sustained identity: 30-second amplified window where all skills fire on reduced cooldowns. No single massive spike like Surge's 60-stack moment — sustained elevated output throughout the 30s window followed by orb rebuild phase.

amp.value: 3-Orb: +48% Attack Power + -50% Cooldown Reduction for 30 seconds; back-attack: +10% Crit Rate +5% Damage
amp.evidence: Maxroll RE guide: '1 Orb: +16% Attack Power; 2 Orbs: +32% Attack Power; 3 Orbs: +48% Attack Power' and '-10/30/50% Cooldown Reduction for 30 seconds.' Directly sourced.

commitment.evidence: RE activation (Surge cast) is fast. The identity is rapid skill spam within the 30s window — skills fire quickly on halved cooldowns. No single committed cast dominates.

mechanics_notes: 1) COOLDOWN HALVING within the 30s window is uniquely powerful: -50% cooldown at 3 Orbs effectively doubles skill frequency → combined with +48% Attack Power = roughly doubling expected DPS for 30 seconds. This is one of the highest identity amplification windows in LA. 2) LOWER MECHANICAL DEMAND than Surge: RE doesn't require 60-stack optimization. The 30s window is easier to manage in raid content — even partial utilization yields consistent output. 3) RE vs SURGE META DELTA: RE is S+-tier (Maxroll Aug 2025) vs Surge's B-tier. The gap opened after the Ark Passive Enlightenment update amplified RE's 30s window mechanics further while Surge's 60-stack requirement remained unforgiving in mobile content. 4) RE Deathblade is consistently listed among LA's top DPS choices as of 2025-2026 — the 'tank-and-sustain' version of the Deathblade identity fork relative to Surge's 'spike-and-pray' design.
